newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAPPI WORKERS PROTEST IN SYMPATHY WITH U.S..
newsitem.headline: SAPPI WORKERS PROTEST IN SYMPATHY WITH U.S..

text.p: About 6,000 employees of South African pulp and paper producer Sappi Ltd will down tools at the company's 12 mills on Friday in sympathy with their U.S. counterparts demanding worker rights, a union spokesman said.

Alfred Tshabalala of the Paper Printing Wood and Allied Workers Union (PPWAWU) said a number of workers at Sappi's U.S. subsidiary, S.D. Warren Somerset mill, in Maine, had been suspended and others threatened with dismissals.

"Tommorrow (Friday) our workers are going to down tools for two hours at all Sappi plants. It's going to be a tough day for Sappi because they are going to lose two hours of production," he told Reuters.
"We are staging this action in support for our American counterparts. Sappi is threatening to dismiss them for demanding their rights," Tshabalala added.
A Sappi spokesman Johan van Wyk said the company was aware of the planned action and did not think it would impact badly on production.
